ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Communications
ns1:channel.ns1:description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

ns1:item.ns1:title: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78300-7

Researchers developed a machine learning model using FDG-PET imaging to accurately predict Alzheimer’s-type tau pathology across spectrums of aging and dementia, providing a novel framework to estimate tau burden non-invasively.
ns1:item.dc:title: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders

ns1:item.ns1:title: AI-accelerated scalable synthesis of nanocrystals for cost-effective photovoltaics
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78268-4

The commercialization of perovskite nanocrystals requires low-cost synthesis and processing. Zhao et al. developed an AI-accelerated framework to optimize the FAPbI3 nanocrystal synthesis under room-temperature, achieving a production cost of US$ 2.16 g−1 with a power conversion efficiency of 19.37%.
ns1:item.dc:title: AI-accelerated scalable synthesis of nanocrystals for cost-effective photovoltaics

ns1:item.ns1:title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77518-9

Subchondral bone remodeling is increasingly implicated in osteoarthritis, but its spatial organization remain incompletely understood. This study provides a high-resolution spatial map of subchondral bone and identifies conserved spatial architectures, revealing distinct microenvironmental states and candidate signaling pathways associated with subchondral bone sclerosis.
ns1:item.dc:title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals microenvironmental heterogeneity in osteoarthritic subchondral bone

ns1:item.ns1:title: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ-driven uveal melanomas
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77999-8

Uveal melanoma (UM) is often driven by mutations in GNAQ. Here, authors identify p300 as a synthetic lethal target in GNAQ-mutant UM and show that p300 inhibition impairs tumour growth and metastasis.
ns1:item.dc:title: Synthetic lethal screens reveal p300/CBP as a vulnerability for GNAQ-driven uveal melanomas

ns1:item.ns1:title: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78190-9

In this study, Jose Molto and colleagues report data from a randomised open-label clinical trial showing of first-line dolutegravir/lamivudine treatment for HIV-1. They report that the treatment reaches lymph nodes and regions containing HIV-positive cells, which strengthens evidence for antiviral exposure within a key anatomical HIV reservoir.
ns1:item.dc:title: First-line dolutegravir/lamivudine in HIV-1 infection: lymph node penetration and reservoir decline in a randomized open-label clinical trial
